[0] everyday_reading (E): Graph paper and screens suggest pixel coordinates, or axes that start wherever the data start. StdDraw's default coordinates are the unit square, and setXscale/setYscale map any chosen ranges onto the canvas.
[1] misconception (M) -> PixelCoordinates: wrong rule: StdDraw.point(256, 256) draws in the middle of the default window. Right rule: In the default unit square the middle is (0.5, 0.5). Use setXscale(0, 512) and setYscale(0, 512) to work in pixel-like units.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> PixelCoordinates: Points to LT (a scale applies to the drawing commands after it). An uneven trace maps some points with the old scale, or applies the x-scale to y. (here mixing in: "StdDraw.point(256, 256) draws in the middle of the default window")

[0] names_the_element (N): Coordinate scaling is done by StdDraw control commands, setXscale(x0, x1) and setYscale(y0, y1), which choose the user-coordinate ranges mapped onto the canvas.
[1] states_the_rule (S): setXscale(x0, x1) followed by setYscale(y0, y1) makes the canvas the box with lower-left corner (x0, y0) and upper-right corner (x1, y1). The no-argument versions reset to the unit square.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The scale calls run first and change the mapping state. Every later drawing command converts its (x, y) through the current mapping. Integer arguments are converted to double.
[1] output_prediction (OP): After setXscale(0, N) and setYscale(0, N), line(0, N-i, i, 0) for i = 0..N draws lines spanning the whole canvas, and (N/2, N/2) is the centre. The methods return void.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One scale call changes only the coordinate mapping for one axis. It draws nothing and leaves the existing picture alone.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The scale fixes how every later StdDraw coordinate is interpreted. The pen radius is unaffected by it.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Before plotting, set the x-scale to the sampled interval and the y-scale to the function's min and max, so the curve fits the canvas.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Scaling matches the drawing to the data, so values can be drawn in their own units.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> PixelCoordinates: Scaling the data and the axis ranges by the same factor leaves the picture the same. The pen radius stays the same whatever the scale.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Set the scales whenever the data's natural range is not [0, 1] (plots, maps such as USA.txt, integer grids). Data already normalized to [0, 1] need no scaling.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Data must fall inside the scaled box to be visible. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: The scale is not set, or set to the wrong range (e.g. the y-range misses the function's min and max), so parts of the plot fall off the canvas.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A scale applies only to drawing done after it. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: setXscale is called after the points are drawn, so they were placed in unit-square coordinates.
